_: Several wordings per court result (say.js; Reigns' fresh deck): the realm never says the same thing twice in a row. Keys are kind.option, and event.* for the chronicle's own news (narrator.js and the realm's lords, sieges, years and the dead); {names} are filled by the court. Add a wording to any list to widen it; a key with none uses the court's own line. reword: the local model (Omni, reword.js) adds a wording a season to the result with the fewest, kept beside the chronicles (on: the switch; most: added wordings kept per result). A line told for several towns at once (famine, plague, barracks: server.js GROUPED) takes the season's wording, so the towns share one line.
grain.order: By royal command, {donor} feeds the starving of {house}, and resents every sack.
{donor}'s granaries open on the King's word. The carts roll to {house}, and {donor} counts each one.
The King makes {donor} feed {house}. {house} eats; {donor} keeps the reckoning in its head.
{donor} sends grain to {house}, because the King said so. Nobody in {donor}'s hall says thank you.
Wagons of {donor}'s wheat reach {house}'s hungry. {donor}'s steward calls it theft with a seal on it.
grain.grant: Royal grain rolls out of Kingsmere for {house}. The bakers there light their ovens again.
The King opens his own stores for {house}. Tonight, {house}'s children eat.
Kingsmere's granary feeds {house} this winter. Its lord will remember who did.
grain.refuse: The King refuses grain. In {house}'s lands, the bannermen begin to talk.
No grain for {house}. Its bannermen eat their seed corn and wonder aloud what a King is for.
The King keeps his granaries shut. {house} tightens its belt, and its bannermen loosen their tongues.
{house} goes hungry by the King's word. Its knights start asking who else might feed them.
informer.reward: {informer} leaves court with a heavier purse. Within the month, {suspect} knows who talked.
The King pays {informer} for the tale. {suspect} hears of it before the coins are spent.
{informer} is rewarded in silver. Court is a small place: {suspect} soon knows whose silver.
Gold for {informer}, a long memory for {suspect}. The two no longer dine at the same table.
informer.dismiss: The King dismisses the accusation. {informer} leaves court red-faced.
The King hears {informer} out, and laughs. The court laughs with him. {informer} does not.
remembers.hear: The King hears {name} out and promises nothing. {house} goes home with its grudge, and it grows.
{name} speaks; the King listens; nothing is promised. {house} rides home angrier than it came.
"We will think on it," says the King. {house} has heard that before. The grudge gets heavier.
{name} is heard to the end, and sent away with nothing. {house}'s old wound opens a little wider.
remembers.purse: {house} sends {gold} gold to Kingsmere. {name} had hoped for thanks, not a reckoning.
{name} came for an apology and leaves {gold} gold lighter. {house} will tell this story for years.
{gold} gold from {house} to the crown, for the trouble of listening. {name} pays, and does not smile.
remembers.firm: "The crown did what it must." {name} bows, and adds it to the account.
The King stands by what was done. {name} bows, and {house} adds a line to its long ledger.
"It was right then and it's right now," says the King. {name} says nothing, which says enough.
The King gives no ground. {name} leaves, already counting what the crown will owe for it.
council.side: The King sides with {winner}. {loser} leaves the council hall without bowing.
The King's word goes to {winner}. {loser}'s lords push back their chairs and walk out.
{winner} has the King's backing. {loser} hears it in silence, and is gone before the wine.
The King rules for {winner}. {loser} does not argue. It simply stops coming to council.
event.founded: Settlers under {house}'s banner raise the first roofs of {town}.
{town} is marked out in the mud, and {house} calls it a town.
event.famine: The granaries are empty and {people} starve.
There is no bread, and {people} eat the seed corn.
The granaries stand empty; {people} go hungry.
Not a sack of grain is left, and {people} grow thin.
event.plague: The dead are carted out by night.
The bells ring for the dead every morning.
Doors are marked with chalk, and the carts come at dusk.
event.barracks: {house} wants more spears, and does not say why.
event.walls: {town} raises walls of stone. {house} expects war.
Masons of {house} wall in {town}. Someone expects trouble.
Stone walls go up round {town}; {house} trusts its neighbours less each year.
event.arena: {house} builds an arena in {town} to quiet the restless crowds.
{house} gives {town} an arena, and the crowds something to shout at.
An arena rises in {town}; {house} would rather the people roar there than at its gates.
event.sept: {house} raises a sept in {town}; the people turn to the gods.
A sept goes up in {town}, paid for by {house}. The people pray louder.
{house} builds the gods a house in {town}.
event.conquest: {town} falls to {to}. {from} loses it in a day.
{to}'s banners fly over {town}; {from}'s are trampled in the gate.
event.razed: {town} is razed to the ground by {house}.
Nothing stands of {town} now. {house} saw to it.
event.death: {name} of {house} dies at {age}. The bells toll in {where}.
{name} of {house} is dead at {age}. {where} goes into mourning.
The bells of {where} ring for {name} of {house}, dead at {age}.
event.alliance: Ravens fly between {house} and {other}. {name} and {othername} speak of friendship.
{name} of {house} sends gifts to {othername} of {other}. Friendship, they call it.
{house} and {other} drink to each other's health. {name} and {othername} mean some of it.
Letters pass between {name} and {othername}. {house} and {other} grow close.
event.court: {name} of {house} rides to Kingsmere with something to say.
{name} of {house} waits on the King's pleasure.
{name} of {house} asks to be heard at court.
event.siege: {house} brings {n} companies against the walls of {town}.
event.year: The year turns. It is {year} AC.
{year} AC: a new year, and the old quarrels with it.
event.deadagain: The dead come again, more than before{often}. The northern houses beg the King for aid.
Again the dead cross the wall, more of them than last time{often}. The North sends riders to Kingsmere.
The dead are back in greater number{often}. The northern lords beg for the King's men.
event.deadheld: The dead broke against the walls of {town}. {lord} held, and {men} of them lie in the snow.
The walls of {town} held against the dead. {lord} leaves {men} of them in the snow.
{lord} held {town}. {men} of the dead lie frozen under its walls.
